transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 4:00 PM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Claire Wong (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Verdant Head of AI), Daniel Ruiz (Verdant Infra Lead), Aisha Khan (Verdant Procurement)
Shared: Renewal deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/verdant-renewal-2026), Benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/verdant-prefix-cache.xlsx)

Summary (auto): Verdant is evaluating a 12-month renewal with a capacity uplift from 8->20 GPUs, wants to add us-west-2 and eu-west-1 regions, and needs contract/PO timeline for procurement. SE recommends a Dedicated reserved pool with burst capacity and prefix KV caching to keep per-token cost down. Security docs (SOC2, ISO, KMS integration) requested.

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. we wanna run through the renewal ask, the additional regions and any infra/security questions. quick intros?
00:12 Maya: hi, Maya here, head of AI at Verdant. still running the main recommender and chat flow through Redwood, pretty happy so far but we have some new SLAs.
00:20 Daniel: Daniel, infra, need to make sure networking and peering works for extra regions and egress isn't crazy.
00:26 Aisha: Aisha from procurement, i'll be handling the PO and contract questions.
00:31 Claire: Claire Wong, SE at Redwood, i'll cover perf implications and benchmarking notes, and give recommendations on reserved pools and batching.
00:40 Samir: Cool. quick context from our side: you mentioned wanting to go from 8 to about 20 GPUs and add two regions, is that still the target?
00:50 Maya: yeah, roughly. Our chat latency budget for premium users is sub-250ms p95 and we want to lower cost per token too. so the 20 GPUs is more of a peak target, we might not always need that steady.
01:05 Claire: okay, so that suggests a mix: reserved capacity for predictable throughput plus burst capacity for peak. we typically recommend pinning the model version and using autoscale with a reserved floor. prefix/KV cache will save a lot depending on repetition in prompts.
01:20 Daniel: can you explain the tradeoff again between dedicated reserved and hosted burst? last time there was some confusion about data residency and routing.
01:30 Claire: yeah, so reserved pools (Dedicated) give you hardware isolation and predictable latency; you pay for the commit but get guaranteed throughput. Burst is best-effort and may route to other compatible variants in the catalog if your pool is saturated - which can slightly change latency and cost. for data residency, Private (VPC) or Dedicated in the region keeps data in-region; hosted API by default is us-central but we can pin region routes.
01:56 Maya: we're leaning on dedicated because of the SLAs, plus we want encryption via our KMS. is KMS integration supported in Dedicated?
02:05 Samir: yes, we support KMS/HSM for keys and can do customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments. we'll include the KMS integration guide in the docs we send.
02:15 Aisha: and SOC2 and ISO reports? need those for procurement.
02:20 Samir: absolutely - SOC2 and ISO certs are in our compliance package. i'll attach them with the pricing email.
02:28 Maya: great. on regions: we want us-west-2 and eu-west-1. what's the lead time to stand up dedicated pools in a new region?
02:38 Claire: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for Dedicated in an existing region if capacity is available; for eu-west-1 it might be closer to 3-5 depending on GPU availability. we can prioritize setup and do an initial pilot in us-west-2 first.
02:52 Daniel: any extra networking steps? we have strict egress limits and need VPC peering plus SAML SSO to our portal.
03:00 Claire: VPC peering and SAML are standard for Dedicated/Private. for egress, we can route and NAT in the customer VPC; i'll note the peering doc. some customers set up a NAT gateway and we coordinate IP allowlists.
03:14 Daniel: ok. performance wise - what's the expected p95 for a 4k context length model on Dedicated with kv cache enabled?
03:22 Claire: depends on kernel and quantization, but ballpark for our optimized runtime: p95 ~ 200-280ms for 4k typical sequences with continuous batching tuned. the KV cache reduces repeated prefixes significantly - so if your rerank/chat uses shared context, latency improves. our benchmarks in the sheet show 220ms p95 for similar workloads. note: there's some variance across GPU types.
03:44 Maya: any options for cheaper runs for background tasks? like lower-cost quantized variants?
03:50 Claire: yes - we can recommend quantized model variants for non-latency-critical workloads, and route those jobs to lower-cost pools. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and batching to minimize cost.
04:02 Aisha: procurement needs to lock contract term and pricing - are there discounts for multi-region reserved capacity?
04:08 Samir: yes, multi-region commits get a tiered discount. also annual commitments have additional savings. i'll put a couple of pricing scenarios in the email: 12-month commit for 20 GPUs with regional add-on, and a 6-month pilot option.
04:20 Maya: timeline then - we need the pricing to start procurement next week, and infra would like at least a two-week window to validate in staging.
04:28 Samir: understood. we'll aim to send pricing + compliance pack by Monday (2026-03-15). are there any blockers on your side for signing?
04:38 Aisha: main open items are pricing, KMS integration details, and PO terms. once pricing okayed, procurement can move fast.
04:45 Daniel: technical blocker could be IP allowlist and peering setup; i'd like a small checklist for infra to follow.
04:52 Claire: i'll add a networking checklist to the benchmark doc, including required ports, peering steps, and recommended NAT config.
04:59 Maya: also want to confirm rollback/fallback behavior if a region has an outage - what does Redwood do?
05:06 Claire: we have smart routing & fallback policies: requests can route to other compatible model variants or regions per your policy. for strict data residency customers, we can do local fallback to a Private deployment or failover to a verified model in-region if allowed. we'll include recommended rollout/fallback configs in the console runbook.
05:24 Samir: alright, let's recap next steps. I'll send pricing + SOC2/ISO + KMS guide by Monday. Claire will send the benchmark spreadsheet with recommended batching and networking checklist. Daniel will confirm peering requirements and target cutover dates for the two regions by next Thursday (2026-03-19). Aisha will prepare procurement checklist and preferred terms.
05:40 Maya: sounds good. any concerns about competitors? we did a quick eval of Anthropic for chat but Redwood's latency and cost profile looked better in our sims.
05:50 Samir: great to hear. i'll include a short competitive note in the pricing doc so procurement sees the differentiation.
05:58 Aisha: one last question - support SLA for Dedicated?
06:02 Samir: Dedicated comes with a 99.9% uptime SLA and an enterprise support tier with 2-hour response for sev1, we can adjust on the contract.
06:12 Daniel: ok. thanks everyone. we'll look for the pack Monday and aim to have procurement started by end of next week.
06:20 Samir: Thanks, appreciate it. we'll follow up with the artifacts and set a pilot kick-off once pricing is approved.
06:26 (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings on technical terms (KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"), speaker labels were mostly correct.
